subject: ventures/window-replacement-bid-calculator
professional: an estimator or owner at a small residential window replacement company who bids insert and full-frame jobs weekly; first checks: are United Inches computed and the call sizes named correctly (a 3040 is 3'0" x 4'0"), is the price built as cost / (1 - margin) and not as a markup, is payroll burden loaded onto the wage, are story access, tear-out, rot and lead-safe (EPA RRP) work priced per opening, and does the printed proposal match the price on screen.

evidence.correctness: Independent Python (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/f091d3e5-eb30-514d-8285-e6f58aa0a1bf/scratchpad/wrbc/indep.py, run with python3 -I, no subject import) rebuilds the bid from the per-opening rates the page itself publishes in its FAQ (hours, $ base, $/UI, frame and install multipliers, 0.75 h / 2.1 h story adders, 90/120 UI size steps) plus textbook margin arithmetic (price = cost / (1 - m), overhead on direct cost). Matches calc.mjs to the cent: index.html default 7-opening job at shipped inputs ($38, 32% burden, 12 mi at 28 mph, 1 h setup, 6 h minimum, $95 trip, $375 scaffold, $85 permit, 15% OH, 25% margin) -> 21.0571 h, cost $4,445.24, price $5,926.99, $846.71/opening (node probe.mjs agrees, second-story labour share 79.69%); vs-page easy job 15.5857 h, $3,071.48, $4,095.30, $511.91; vs-page hard job (with the per-row Trim flag the test sets) 71.5857 h, $14,107.24, $18,809.65, $2,351.21, gaps $10,011.94 / $14,714.35; FAQ markup-vs-margin $8,000 -> $9,600 = 16.67% margin vs $10,000 at 20% margin; README '$38 costs more like $50' = 38 x 1.32 = $50.16. Arithmetic is right. Edge findings: story 2.5 silently gets the third-storey 2.1 h adder; fractional quantities (0.5 window) accepted; an unknown unit type silently prices as double-hung. Not 4: the size constants are mislabelled against trade call sizes (see domain) and the edges above.
evidence.completeness: README claims: per-opening takeoff (UI, qty, story, frame, install, condition), loaded labour, disposal/scaffold/trip/permit/casing/capping, overhead, margin, average per opening, effective hourly rate, labour split, second-story share, walk-away price, proposed-price check, copy summary, print quote, share link, usage tally with DNT/GPC opt-out. All present in calc.mjs / index.html: all seven usage events are wired in index.html (grep counts 3,1,1,1,1,1,1), add-on checkboxes at index.html:216-217, DNT/GPC at usage.mjs:21, proposal panel with deposit split and signature line (proposal.mjs). `node --test '*.test.mjs'` 129/129 pass in 0.24 s. Served copy (`node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs window-replacement-bid-calculator`) builds with no placeholder origin; the live host returned 000 through the proxy. Limits (no tax, no tempered/egress/impact glass, no crew size) are disclosed in README Limitations.
evidence.verification: 129 tests green. quality_mutate.py, 9 mutants in core logic: caught 5 (LARGE_UI > -> >=, 2nd-storey 0.75 -> 0.7 h, needsAccess story >= 2 -> > 2, Trim hours scaled by frame multiplier, second-story share filter >= 2 -> > 2); survived 4 (OVERSIZE_UI boundary > -> >= at calc.mjs:81, proposed-price hourly rate divided by on-site instead of total hours at calc.mjs:276, minimum-hours flag < -> <= at calc.mjs:214, proposal deposit Math.round -> Math.floor at proposal.mjs:330). The 120 UI boundary and the proposed-price block (a displayed number the contractor decides on) are unpinned. The vs-page test pins the worked example to calc.mjs but uses hand-picked inputs while the page calls them 'shipped', and no test compares them with index.html's defaults, which is how that overclaim survived. 5 of 9: 2.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (300 lines), index.html script block (lines 378-700), share.mjs, usage.mjs, proposal.mjs header, the four test files. calc.mjs is pure, documented, validates every number with a named error, keeps margin and overhead definitions explicit, and returns intermediate lines for display. Defects: presetById silently falls back to double-hung/vinyl/insert/clean for an unknown id (calc.mjs:69) instead of erroring, so a stale share link with a renamed preset re-prices quietly; story is not forced to an integer (2.5 -> third-storey adder) and quantity not to a whole number; a per-row 'Trim' checkbox (0.35 h, $42, calc.mjs:20-21) sits beside a job-wide 'Interior casing / returns' add-on (0.4 h, $38) with no text saying how they differ, and the vs-page worked example turns both on; proposal.mjs is a byte-identical copy in 121 ventures (md5 088181e3...), guarded by a sync check but still a copied engine. A senior reviewer would accept it with those notes.
evidence.claims: Pass: disclaimer ('No warranty', index.html:370) on the tool and the comparison pages; 'nothing uploaded' (no fetch in index.html, share link is the hash only); usage events list matches index.html; worked example numbers reproduce from calc.mjs; vs-marketsharp carries a not-affiliated clause; served llms.txt lists all four pages on marisstella.app. Fail: (1) the 3040/6048 call sizes are given as 70 UI and 108 UI on index.html:12 and :318-321, how-much-to-charge.html:11, :30, :50, and calc.mjs:9 - by the US trade call-size convention a 3040 is 3'0" x 4'0" = 36 + 48 = 84 UI and a 6048 is 6'0" x 4'8" = 72 + 56 = 128 UI (oversize by the tool's own 120 UI step), so the page teaches the reader a wrong UI for the two sizes it names; (2) vs-a-flat-price-per-window.html:11, :81 and :116 call its inputs 'this calculator's own shipped cost inputs/defaults' ($32 wage, 28% burden, $150 scaffold, 12% OH, and undisclosed 35 mph, 0.5 h setup, 0 h minimum, $0 trip, $0 permit), but index.html ships $38, 32%, $375, 15%, 28 mph, 1 h, 6 h, $95, $85 (index.html:209-232); at the true shipped inputs the easy job is $4,752.50 / $594.06 per window, not $4,095.30 / $511.91. Unit prices and hours are uncited 'ballpark' figures, disclosed as such.
evidence.fitness: Job walked: an estimator enters the default house (picture, four 2nd-floor bedrooms, slider, 2nd-floor casement with rot), sets wage and burden, and gets $5,926.99, $846.71 per opening, 79.7% of labour on the second storey, a walk-away of $4,445.24, a proposed-price check, and a printable proposal with a 30% deposit split and a signature line - a real bid can go out in minutes on the contractor's own rates. Gaps a working estimator hits: no sales tax line (disclosed), no crew-size input (hours are labour-hours at one wage), linear $/UI material rather than the UI brackets distributors actually quote, no tempered/egress/obscure glass options (disclosed), and the default material rates are uncited. Usable with stated limits: 3.
evidence.domain: Compared against trade practice: United Inches = width + height (correct); call sizes in feet-and-inches (3040 = 36 x 48 in) - departs, the tool and its pages treat the four digits as inches; margin as a share of price and overhead on direct cost (correct, the FAQ example is right); payroll burden ~32% on wage (in the usual 25-40% range for construction trades); EPA RRP (40 CFR 745 Subpart E) lead-safe work for pre-1978 homes priced as an adder and explicitly not a compliance finding (sound); scaffold as a job-level cost triggered by any opening at storey 2+ (sound). Departures: the call-size error above, which also means the '6048 picture at 108 UI' example is classed 'large' when a real 6048 is oversize; distributor UI pricing is usually bracketed, not linear past a 70 UI base; IRC R308 safety glazing and R310 egress are not modelled (disclosed); the Trim vs interior-casing overlap invites double counting. A senior estimator would correct the call-size teaching before signing off: 2.

defects.what: Call sizes are read as inches: the tool page, the 'how much to charge' guide and calc.mjs say a 3040 is 70 UI and a 6048 picture is 108 UI. By the trade convention a 3040 is 3'0" x 4'0" = 84 UI and a 6048 is 6'0" x 4'8" = 128 UI (oversize by the tool's own 120 UI step). The FAQ teaches the reader a wrong UI and calls the 70 UI base 'a stock 3040'.

The comparison page calls its worked-example inputs 'this calculator's own shipped cost inputs/defaults', but they differ from every shipped default (wage, burden, scaffold, overhead, speed, setup, minimum hours, trip fee, permit); at the real shipped inputs the easy job is $4,752.50 ($594.06/window), not $4,095.30 ($511.91). Five of the differing inputs are not disclosed on the page.
4 of 9 seeded mutants survive: the 120 UI oversize boundary, the proposed-price hourly rate, the minimum-hours flag boundary and the proposal deposit rounding are not pinned by any test.

Silent fallbacks and loose input: an unknown unit/frame/install/condition id silently prices as the default preset (a stale share link re-prices quietly); story 2.5 gets the third-storey adder; fractional quantities are accepted.

Per-row 'Trim' (0.35 h, $42) and the job-wide 'Interior casing / returns' add-on (0.4 h, $38) overlap with no text separating them; the vs-page example turns both on, which double counts casing labour if they are the same scope.

Starting unit prices, hours and adders are uncited ballparks and material is linear per UI past 70, whereas distributors usually quote UI brackets; disclosed as ballpark but no source or date for any rate.

verdict: A clean, pure bid engine whose arithmetic is right: an independent Python rebuild from the page's own published rates matches calc.mjs to the cent on the default seven-opening house ($5,926.99, walk-away $4,445.24), both comparison-page jobs ($4,095.30 and $18,809.65) and the margin-vs-markup FAQ, and the product does what its README lists, including a printable proposal; 129 tests pass. It misses the bar on claims and verification, and domain sits at 2: the pages teach that a 3040 is 70 UI and a 6048 is 108 UI when the trade call-size convention gives 84 and 128; the comparison page presents hand-picked inputs as 'this calculator's own shipped defaults' when every one differs from index.html; 4 of 9 seeded mutants survive, including the 120 UI boundary and the proposed-price block; unknown presets fall back silently; and the default rates are uncited.
